title: Bajaj Housing Finance Ltd - 544252 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Bajaj Housing Finance Q4 FY26 PAT rose 14% to INR669 crore (20% ex one-time tax benefit), with AUM up 23% and GNPA steady at 27 bps.
summary.overview: AUM crossed INR140,000 crore, growing 23% YoY, with quarterly AUM additions of INR7,294 crore and disbursements up 23% YoY to INR17,506 crore. Spreads compressed 10 bps QoQ to 1.7% and NIM fell 12 bps to 3.8% on lower acquisition yields and a 15 bps PLR pass-through in December. Asset quality held (GNPA 27 bps, NNPA 11 bps), but annualised credit cost rose to 19 bps from 11 bps YoY on a deliberate Stage 2 provision top-up. Management guided to ROA compression of about 10 bps in FY27 (towards upper end of the 2.0-2.2% medium-term range) assuming no policy rate change, and said it will firm up guidance with Q1 results.

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: AUM grew 18% YoY and is 54.1% of AUM (management said regulatory IHL ratio is 50.45%). Home loan GNPA rose 1 bp to 35 bps; yields estimated at 8.5-8.6% on book, incremental 8.05-8.10%.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: AUM grew 24% YoY, 10.8% of mix, up 10 bps QoQ. LAP GNPA fell 6 bps to 46 bps; on-book yield about 150 bps above home loans.

segments.name: Lease rental discounting (LRD)
segments.commentary: AUM grew 44% YoY, 22.4% of mix, up 50 bps QoQ. Nil GNPA; yield about 7.9-8.0%, lower-margin product.

segments.name: Developer finance (DF) / construction finance
segments.commentary: DF AUM grew 13% YoY (11.5% mix) as funded projects generate higher cash flows. Highest-margin product; yield about 11.5-11.75%. Construction finance GNPA flat at 3 bps.

segments.name: Sambhav (near prime and affordable)
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursements of INR410-425 crore in Q4, targeting INR600 crore+ within 12 months. AUM about INR9,000 crore (mix roughly 70:30 affordable to near prime); ATS INR28 lakh, 68% salaried, about 65% with CIBIL above 750. Operates in 73 locations.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ROA expected towards upper end of the 2.0-2.2% medium-term range, with about 10 bps ROA compression assumed from NIM pressure; partly offset by opex efficiency and lower credit cost.
Q1 FY27 yields expected broadly sideways to slightly lower; cost of funds to fall 2-3 bps QoQ, helped by NHB refinance resets and maturing high-cost NCDs.
Assumes no repo hike; no further PLR cut envisaged. If policy rate is hiked, management expects partial pass-through (10-20 bps) and no margin compression.
AUM growth ambition of 21-23% for FY27 with growth at about 2x industry; assignment income to be used as a balancing lever depending on home loan BT-out.
Full-year assessment and detailed guidance to be given with Q1 FY27 results.
capex_capacity: Sambhav run-rate expected to reach INR600 crore+ monthly disbursements within the next 12 months.
Borrowing mix: money market 49%, bank 41%, NHB refinance 10%; floating-rate borrowings 63% including OIS swaps; relationships with 18 banks; AAA/Stable rating.
Recent 3-year NCD coupon at 7.6% fixed, swapped to floating near repo (around 7%).
demand_pricing: Competitive intensity high in prime housing, especially Feb-Mar 2026; PSU banks and private banks cut pricing; SBI and HDFC described as rate setters.
BT-out rate unchanged from Q3 at about 10% of AUM (total attrition about 20%); largest BT-out destination is public sector banks. Management expects BT-out to decline from May if rates stay stable.
Industry IHL growth about 9.5% per latest data; company targets 21-23% growth.
Acquisition yields fell in Q4; portfolio yield down 14 bps QoQ from lower acquisition pricing and attrition of higher-rate book.
Bounce metrics (first bounce, early bounce, 12-month bounce) reportedly improving QoQ through March; April bounce trends described as same.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin fall 12 bps and what is the outlook for Q1 yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower acquisition pricing and the full impact of the 15 bps PLR pass-through from December drove the decline. Q1 yields expected broadly sideways with slight compression; cost of funds to fall 3-5 bps in Q1 per the CFO, later framed as 2-3 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 ROA likely to stay above the medium-term guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 ROA should be at the upper end of the 2.0-2.2% range, with about 10 bps compression from NIM pressure; leverage lifts ROE but not ROA. Full guidance to follow with Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cut PLR further?
qa_highlights.answer: No further PLR cut envisaged absent a repo change; money market rates are elevated, with OIS pricing about 75 bps of hikes, which management says it does not fully believe.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Stage 2 coverage raised and are early bounce trends deteriorating?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bounce metrics are improving QoQ across segments and April is the same; the Stage 2 coverage increase was a prudential top-up given the macro environment, with no micro stress.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sambhav AUM and its near-prime/affordable mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Sambhav AUM is close to INR9,000 crore, roughly 70:30 between affordable and near prime; exact split to be confirmed later.

qa_highlights.question: Will fee and assignment income keep growing faster than loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income rose to INR297 crore from INR200 crore, driven by insurance and foreclosure income. Assignment income is a balancing lever and fee income is expected to grow in line with the business.

risks_watch: Money market and NCD rates remain elevated; if policy rates are not hiked, the company absorbs the cost increase and margins compress (about 10 bps ROA).
Home loan BT-out by PSU banks and private banks; IHL ratio close to the 50% regulatory floor (50.45%), with some management comfort from the monthly compliance record.
Credit cost of 19 bps in Q4 reflects a Stage 2 provision top-up; the sustainability of the 2-3 bps Q4 uplift is unclear.
Development finance AUM growth slowed to 13%, and DF cash flows could further affect the mix.
Sambhav scaling to INR600 crore monthly disbursements and the near prime/affordable mix (not yet confirmed) need tracking.
Macro and geopolitical volatility referenced by management as making forward guidance uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics and asset quality, but noticeably cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly declined to give firm FY27 margin guidance before Q1 and framed rate scenarios conditionally. Most hedged on rate-hike pass-through and when the money market normalises.
key_quotes: There is no single month till now in our history where we have not maintained the regulatory requirement.
It should be towards the upper end of the medium term guidance may not beat that.
Q4 is normally a high competitive intensity market and the yields , the acquisition prices come down to a certain extent, but it is also resulting from a change of a mix.
Purely from a prudence point of view from the current market current macro environment. No micro input has gone in this.
So, there is no pass-through further is what can be envisaged in the current scenario.
But we'll come with the full guidance in the quarter 1 along with the quarter 1 results.

adds.what: Sambhav near-prime/affordable disbursement ramp to INR600 crore+ monthly (run-rate INR410-425 crore/month in Q4; 73 locations today)

growth.why: Management reiterated AUM growth of 21-23% for FY27 (about 2x industry IHL growth of ~9.5%), backed by disbursements up 23% YoY and Sambhav scaling toward INR600 crore+ monthly within 12 months, though no specific new capacity or order book was quantified and ROA is guided to compress ~10 bps.
